subject: BrightLayer adapter v2 migration — request for migration kit and extended support
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@brightlayer.io>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Devon Park <devon@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: BrightLayer adapter v2 — migration timeline and resources

Hi Neha,

Quick note from BrightLayer: we’re planning to ship Adapter v2 for our connector that consumes Redwood’s inference API in Q1. Our engineering lead has flagged a couple of breaking surface changes: a reworked /v1/predict payload (new batching header, tokenization hint) and removal of synchronous stream fallbacks.

To avoid forcing our customers into a last-minute fork, can Redwood provide: 
- a migration kit (sample client shims and tests),
- a compatibility matrix showing where behavior will differ, and
- a short-term extended-support SLA (30–60d) after v2 GA while we finish customer migrations.

Can you loop in the right folks? We’d like to publish a migration guide paired to a recommended Redwood release window — ideally the week of Feb 8.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, BrightLayer
attachments: brightlayer-migration-request-20261115.eml

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex@brightlayer.io>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLayer adapter v2 — migration timeline and resources

Alex — thanks for the heads up and detail. We definitely want BrightLayer to have a smooth migration. I’ll coordinate an engineering-owned migration kit and a compatibility matrix.

Next steps from my side:
1) Marcus / Jonas — can you review the API change notes Alex mentioned and estimate effort for a migration kit + example shim (Node + Python) + CI tests?
2) Alex — can you share the exact v2 schema and any sample payloads (or a private postman/collection link)?
3) We’ll assess impact to hosted routes and whether a temporary server-side compatibility flag is feasible for the requested support window.

I’m happy to schedule a 30-min tech sync this week if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0194

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, Alex Mercer <alex@brightlayer.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLayer adapter v2 — migration timeline and resources

Neha / Alex — I pulled the note into an internal ticket and did a quick skim of the changes. A few clarifying questions before we scope the migration kit: 

- "new batching header": is this purely client-side (per-call header) or do you expect server-side routing/batching behavior changes? If server routing changes are needed we’ll need to map to our smart-routing layer.
- the "tokenization hint": do you plan to send a Huffman/byte-token hint or just a short lcm_tokenizer identifier? If the latter we can add a light mapping layer in the shim.
- removal of synchronous stream fallbacks: do you need help implementing a local shim that converts streaming-only responses to a buffered sync API for older clients? We can supply an example pattern.

Work estimate (rough): migration kit + Node + Python shims + CI tests + compat matrix — 5 engineer-days if it’s client-only; 12 engineer-days if server routing changes are required. Deliverable would be a repo with example code, tests, a CHANGELOG, and a compat-matrix.xlsx.

I’ll draft a minimal migration-kit PR (WIP) and drop the initial artifacts in a shared Drive folder by EOD Friday (2026-11-19).

—Marcus Lin
Senior Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex@brightlayer.io>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-17T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLayer adapter v2 — migration timeline and resources

Alex / Team — quick commercial note while Marcus builds the kit. BrightLayer’s ask for a 30–60 day extended-support SLA is doable, but we need to formalize terms. Options:

A) 30 days of extended support included free for verified migrations (limited to BL customers who complete the migration using the kit).
B) 60 days of extended support as a paid add-on (monthly fee or short-term uplift tied to BL’s partner discount schedule).

If you prefer A we’ll include a short addendum and a commitment from Redwood to preserve the old sync behavior behind a compatibility flag for the stated period. If B, I can draft a short SOW and pricing.

Also — can we get an estimated count of BrightLayer customers on the current adapter? That helps quantify the support window and any potential quota/backfill.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Partner Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <alex@brightlayer.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Devon Park <devon@acme.ai>, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: BrightLayer adapter v2 — migration timeline and resources

Thanks, everyone — really appreciate the quick response and the concrete plan. Short answers:
- We expect ~14 customers on the existing adapter in production (mix of startups and a handful of mid-market).
- The batching header is client-side only; we will not change server routing. The tokenization hint is a short identifier string (e.g., "bll-sentence-v2").
- We would like the example shim that converts streaming responses to buffered sync for legacy clients — that will be the highest immediate value.

We are happy to accept Option A (30 days free) to reduce friction. If we need the 60-day window we’ll discuss a short SOW.

Next steps agreed:
1) Marcus to share the initial migration-kit PR + compat-matrix.xlsx by EOD Friday (2026-11-19).
2) Ben to draft a 1-paragraph addendum preserving the sync behavior behind a compatibility flag for 30 days post-GA.
3) Neha to schedule a tech sync for next Tuesday to walk through the shim pattern.

I’ve attached our initial schema examples and a short Postman collection.

Regards,
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, BrightLayer
attachments: migration-kit-request-samples.postman_collection.json, sample-schema-v2.json
